feasible.reason: The repo evidence is accurate (no PVD/ADC4 driver anywhere in secure/src; shared/src/lockdown.rs:518-522 keeps BOR_LEV advisory; secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:285-322 arms ITAMP7/12/13 in CR3=0 confirmed mode with no ADC4 behind them; secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:244-246 defers the BOR check; gh #48/#49/#208/#248 all OPEN; Trezor pvd.c uses PVD level 5 and option_bytes.c forces OB_BOR_LEVEL_4 with the ADC watchdogs 'never triggered'). Parts (a), (b) and (d) are firmware/option-byte work that genuinely bounds the dwell window of slow (µs-class) supply attacks and raises the cost of a USB-supply attacker; the proposal is already honest that ns crowbars are not caught, and the µ-Glitch text I extracted confirms the shape (400 ns glitch split into 170+140 ns to evade a sampling BoD, at a lower success rate; on the STM32L5 they had to glitch the PLL config to neutralise the BoD). So the proposal is not refuted as a bar-raiser. It is, however, wrong in several load-bearing details: BOR-4 and PVD-5 sit at the SAME threshold on this part, so the PVD→zeroize handler races the BOR reset and is not guaranteed to run; the ADC4/VREFINT analog-watchdog leg (c) cannot resolve glitches (tS_vrefint ≥ 12.65 µs) and is NS-bypassable until GTZC2/TAMPSEC are wired; the VBUS watchdog needs a hardware change the proposal does not flag; and routing a voltage-sag detector into the seed-destroying intrusion wipe (which itself performs a flash write while VDD is sagging) is a bricking design.
feasible.corrections:
1. BOR-4 vs PVD-5 are coincident on STM32U585 (DS13086 Rev 10, 'Embedded reset and power control' table): VBOR4 rising 2.76/2.88/3.0 V, falling 2.67/2.79/2.9 V; VPVD5 rising 2.76/2.88/3.0 V, falling 2.66/2.78/2.9 V; 80 mV hysteresis each. With BOR_LEV=4 + PVDLS=5 the PVD interrupt and the BOR reset fire at the same voltage, so 'PVD → zeroize_sensitive_state + relock' is a race the handler may never win. Trezor can afford this because its handler is just error_shutdown. Pick an ordered pair: BOR-3 (falling typ 2.50 V, already the target in docs/security/brownout-hardening.md:311) + PVD-5 (falling typ 2.78 V), or BOR-4 + PVD-6 (falling typ 2.88 V). BOR-3 is also the safer value to freeze forever at RDP-2 given VBOR4 rising max is 3.0 V on a 3.3 V LDO rail fed from a USB host that may sag to 4.4 V VBUS.
2. PVD handler must be SRAM-only: no flash write, no SE I2C (the SE rail VDD1_3V3 behind PA8 is sagging too). Note that a BOR reset already lands on a cortex-m-rt .bss re-zero plus the ResetCause path (secure/src/reset_cause.rs:182), so PVD adds a pre-reset wipe window, not a new guarantee.
3. Part (c) on VREFINT adds essentially nothing against FI: DS13086 Table 37 gives tS_vrefint = 12.65 µs minimum sampling time, so an ADC4 AWD on VREFINT averages over ~13 µs per conversion, slower than PVD and blind to 100-400 ns glitches. The ADC4 internal VCORE channel (exposed by embassy-stm32's adc4 driver for U5) is the more relevant rail but shares the same sampling floor. Its only real value is a second, hardware-consequenced (TAMP) detector for slow attacks; downgrade (c) from P0 to P2 and from the FI claim to 'supply-integrity tamper'.
4. (c) is NS-bypassable as the branch stands: ADC4 is an SRD-domain peripheral under GTZC2 (the U5 SVD's GTZC2_TZSC SECCFGR carries the SRD ADC bit; CLAUDE.md and secure/src/sau.rs:672-673 say GTZC2 is intentionally NOT configured), secure/src/hw/tamp.rs sets no TAMP_SECCFGR/TAMPSEC, and PVD configuration must be locked with PWR_SECCFGR.VDMSEC. Prerequisite: wire GTZC2 (ADC4 + TAMP + PWR voltage-monitor security) before any of (b)/(c) is load-bearing — that pre-existing GTZC2 gap also means NS can disable the tampers already armed today.
5. The VBUS watchdog is kind=hardware, not firmware: pq1's VBUS sense is PA9 into OTG (secure/src/board/pq1.rs:295-296, a digital AF10 input, not an ADC4 channel) and no free bonded pad (PA10, PC13, PB4; PA6 is NC and taken by the consumption mask) is an ADC4 input, so an analog VBUS monitor needs a divider to an ADC4-capable pin on a board spin. Relabel the proposal kind=mixed.
6. Do not route ITAMP7/12/13 (or PVD) into the destructive wipe. Under tamp-wipe, a confirmed tamper calls secure/src/hw/tzic.rs:228 trigger_intrusion_wipe → arm_wipe_flag on page 125 → next boot factory-resets BOTH SEs (seed halves gone). A voltage-sag detector feeding that path bricks wallets on marginal hosts/cables, and step 2 is a flash write executed during the sag (torn quadword / ECC on page 125). Route supply events to zeroize + relock + a persistent tally; reserve the SE wipe for corroborated events (e.g. two independent detectors or repeated trips), and resolve #208 (ITAMP9 false trips under SAES/BHK) first, as the proposal notes.
7. BOR_LEV field (FLASH_OPTR bits 10:8, shift 8 / mask 7 in lockdown.rs:261-262) is correct, so making bor_lev_ok load-bearing in SHIP_PROFILE_U585, the FSBL tz-1 tripwire and first-boot Phase A is straightforward; remember it freezes at RDP-2 and must be characterised on pq1 across hosts before being pinned.
8. Cost/priority: (a)+(b)+(d) are S-M firmware and legitimately P0 (already ship-blocker #49/#48); (c) with the GTZC2/TAMPSEC prerequisites plus host/cable characterisation is M-L for a slow-attack-only gain. 'Only raises cost, does not prevent' applies to the whole item.
